subject: Acme rerank model fit — next steps & benchmark artifacts
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Acme rerank model fit — next steps & benchmark artifacts

Hi John & Lisa,

Great to chat this morning for walking through the rerank use cases and the examples you shared. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Summary of fit: based on the sample queries and labels you shared in the call, our quick offline runs show the Redwood-rerank-7b-quant (4-bit) gives the best uplift vs your current baseline (Llama2-rerank-3b-finetuned) on the initial holdout: NDCG@10 +0.048, MRR +0.031. These are preliminary — see attached PDF for the top-line numbers and the per-query breakdown in the spreadsheet.

2) Recommended artifacts to validate:
   - Prompt set (attached: prompt_set_v2.csv) includes the production prompt variations and negative sampling used in evaluation.
   - Per-query NDCG/MRR breakdown (attached: acme_ndcg_mrr_breakdown.xlsx).
   - Evaluation harness & scripts (link below) we’ll run the same harness against your full 10k labeled set.

3) Proposed validation / A/B plan:
   - Offline validation run on your 10k labeled set (we can run this in Dedicated infra or we can provide the scripts for you to run).
   - If offline looks good, a staged A/B in production: 2-week test, start at 5% exposure -> 20% -> 50% (if metrics are stable). Primary metrics: NDCG@10 (target uplift +0.05), MRR (target uplift +0.03), and CTR/secondary business metric monitoring.

4) Questions / asks from your side:
   - Can you confirm the labeled set we discussed (10k queries) and provide S3 link or shared Drive?
   - Any latency SLO constraints for the rerank stage (p95 target)?

I’ve attached the initial benchmark PDF and the prompt set. Next step: if you confirm the labeled dataset location, we’ll schedule the offline run and loop in David + Vivek on infra and A/B rollout.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.example
Attachments: prompt_set_v2.csv (text/csv), acme_rerank_initial_ndcg_mrr.pdf (application/pdf)

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 13:22:18 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme rerank model fit — next steps & benchmark artifacts

Thanks Marissa for the recap. A couple quick clarifications: 

- The NDCG/MRR numbers you quoted are on which holdout time window? Are these from the most recent month or aggregated?
- We’d like the evaluation scripts so our ML infra can reproduce the run. Can you share the harness and Dockerfile or a runnable notebook?
- For the A/B plan, is the 2-week window based on statistical power estimates you ran, or a rules-of-thumb? We’ll need to sync with product on exposure cadence.

We can share the labeled 10k as an S3 bucket. I’ll get that link to you by EOD. Also our p95 target for rerank is 120ms.

—John
John Doe
Product Manager, Acme Corp
john.doe@acme.com

Thanks John — answers inline below and next steps.

- Window: the numbers in the PDF are aggregated over the last 30 days from the sample you shared (we used time-sliced sampling to avoid leakage). I’ll include per-day breakdowns in the spreadsheet.
- Harness & reproducibility: attached is the per-query NDCG/MRR breakdown (acme_ndcg_mrr_breakdown.xlsx). Evaluation harness is in the Drive link below (Dockerfile + run scripts). If you want, David can run the job in Dedicated infra and share the exact container we used.
- A/B power: 2-week is a pragmatic window based on your traffic shape. We ran a power estimate (linked) for detecting the stated NDCG uplift (0.05) with your weekly query volume; details in the A/B plan. We can extend if product prefers a longer test.

Proposed immediate next steps:
  1) John — drop the S3 link for the 10k labeled set.
  2) We (Redwood) will run an offline validation (David + Vivek own infra) and return per-query results + failure analysis.
  3) If offline checks pass, schedule A/B with the rollout cadence above.

Drive links & artifacts:
- Benchmarks & harness: https://drive.redwood.company/drive/acme/rerank-benchmarks
- HubSpot (deal): HubSpot: 6291-ACME-Deal

I’ve attached the more detailed spreadsheet with per-query scores. I’ll also draft the A/B plan and share in the thread.

Best,
Marissa
Attachments: acme_ndcg_mrr_breakdown.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.example>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme rerank model fit — next steps & benchmark artifacts

Looping in infra notes — I can run the offline validation on Dedicated this week. A few infra/ops items to call out so Marissa and John have visibility:

- Environment: we’ll use the quantized Redwood-rerank-7b-quant container (same kernels as the PDF). I recommend batch_size=32 for rerank stage and enable prefix KV caching for recurrent sessions.
- Latency: with batching and ashare configs I expect p95 ~110-130ms depending on seq length; we’ll publish exact p95 with the run. If we need <120ms p95 consistently at 50% traffic, we should consider a 7b->3b fallback policy in rollout.
- Data handling: please provide S3 read-only role for the run; we’ll write outputs to a temp bucket for your team to pick up.

I’ll kick off the run once John shares the S3 link.

—David
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick note: we should include regression monitoring hooks for: NDCG@10 delta by query decile, hallucination/score drift alerts, and automatic rollback triggers if business metric falls below threshold. I’ll post the run plan (rerank_ab_plan.md) to the Drive and link here once created.

Vivek
